newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-EDBERG GIVES FANS A FAREWELL EXHIBITION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG GIVES FANS A FAREWELL EXHIBITION.

text.p: Stefan Edberg of Sweden made an emotional farewell to a storied 15-year career in professional tennis last year but on Saturday night he was back on court for an exhibition match in Atlanta.
"I've definitely retired from the ATP Tour but I'll still play some exhibitions," said Edberg, ranked No.1 in the world for 72 weeks between 1990-92 and the owner of six Grand Slam titles.

The Atlanta event, the Aetna US Healthcare Super Showdown, was billed as a Davis-Cup style encounter between the United States and Sweden but was more like a friendly hit and giggle between four former foes. Edberg and countryman, Mats Wilander, took on American legends, Jimmy Connors and John McEnroe in four singles and a doubles set. Each set was best of eight games.
Edberg retired last November after playing his final match in his homeland, a losing first round effort in Stockholm to fellow Swede, Nicklas Kulti.

Edberg, now 31, walked away from the sport with 41 singles titles and 18 doubles championships as well as a reputation which earned him frequent sportsmanship awards and enormous popularity worldwide.

"I still enjoy playing tennis and I still practice a little," said Edberg, who defeated Connors 5-3 and McEnroe 5-4 in his two singles matches. Wilander lost twice in singles and the Americans prevailed in doubles to win the best of five-set format 5-2.
"I had an opportunity to be here and people still want me to play so there's nothing wrong with that," Edberg said.

"It's okay when it's fun and relaxing and nice to be around players I know. On the tour if you get to talk to a player that's a big achievement. They're so protected. Here we interact with fans and sponsors and that's important to build the game."
